messages:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: Paging oncall: elevated 503/429 on HF artifact endpoints for ap-southeast-1. Affected: model-fetcher service. Pager assigned to rotation: nina.

nina: got it. seeing rapid spike in 429s from huggingface artifacts when trying to pull weights for private deployments. starts around 09:07 UTC.

lisa: here's a tail from model-fetcher:
```
2026-03-15T09:07:12Z model-fetcher ERROR fetch hf://org/xlm-60b shard-03 503 "Service Unavailable"
2026-03-15T09:07:13Z model-fetcher WARN retrying fetch (attempt=3) backoff=6s
2026-03-15T09:07:14Z model-fetcher ERROR fetch hf://org/xlm-60b shard-03 429 "Too Many Requests" Retry-After: 8
```

dan: customer impact: several Dedicated cold-starts timed out during model load. Affected customers: two mid-market tenants in APAC. No data plane exposures.

jay: we have a pre-warmed disk cache but a lot of instances were scaled down overnight so they hit cold path. Prefetch failure rate jumped from 0.2% -> 7%.

nina: immediate mitigations I'm applying now:
- reduce parallel fetches per node 12->4
- enable aggressive local disk cache for 30m
- mark ap-southeast-1 as "prefer smaller-variant" in routing rules
rolling changes in k8s now.

rob: I'll open HF support ticket and also flip on our artifact-proxy fallback (internal CDN that pulls from HF). Proxy adds ~200ms overhead but reduces direct HF calls.

lisa: creating HF ticket: attaching sample logs + time window. HF ticket ref: HF-79011. Also linked to status: https://status.huggingface.co/incidents/def456

incident-bot: Note: auto-silenced noisy alerts for model-fetcher errors during mitigation window.

dan: customer comms: starting message draft for affected tenants. Include note that we're routing to smaller variants and prefetching where possible.

jay: adding metric tags: hf.artifact_error=true and hf.retry_after header present to span traces. Also increasing sampling for failing traces.

rob: proxy enabled for ap-southeast-1. Initial results: 429s dropped from ~12% -> ~4% in 5m.

nina: also enabling temporary fallback to xlm-13b for new cold-starts for 45m window. updating rollout config.

lisa: HF support replied: "we're throttling artifact endpoints in apac due to edge congestion; scaling is in progress. Recommend respecting Retry-After and reducing burst concurrency." No exact ETA.

dan: action items:
- rob: maintain HF ticket and escalate if no improvement in 30m
- nina: monitor metrics and revert after stable 15m
- jay: update dashboards + alert thresholds for hf.retry_after spikes
- lisa: send targeted customer notification and include workaround steps

rob: HF says edges are scaling; nightly traffic spike caused cache churn. Asking HF for mitigation timeline and whether they can pre-warm edges for our org.

jay: heatmap shows prefetch failures mostly between 09:05-09:25 UTC. We'll keep proxy for 1 hour then reassess.

nina: measured impact: time-to-ready for new sessions improved by 40% after reduced concurrency + proxy.

lisa: comms sent to affected customers with support instructions. No escalations yet.

incident-bot: Status update: mitigating -> partial service restoration. Pager still active.

rob: handing off to next oncall @dan in 30m if still active. Preparing post-incident notes.

dan: will draft postmortem focusing on: dependency SLAs, prewarm policies, runbook: auto-reduce concurrency + enable proxy + route to smaller variant + open HF ticket + notify customers.

nina: will keep the temporary settings for 45m then gradually revert.

rob: HF updated ticket: edges healthy in most apac POPs; residual throttling cleared. Marking as monitoring.

incident-bot: Incident resolved: HF artifact edges stable, internal proxy stopped being required. Pager closed. Thanks everyone for the quick mitigation.
